title: Multi-Tenant Database Security Lab reference solution notes
review_notes: Illustrative solution outline kept in the repository only. It is not served by the public project endpoint; review actual schema/query behavior before publication.
approach: Start with an ER model and define the row grain for each table. Implement multi-tenant database security lab using primary/foreign keys, CHECK/UNIQUE/NOT NULL rules, and parameterized queries as appropriate. Add synthetic seed rows, then validate result sets and negative cases.
reference_sql:
-- Begin with a copy of datasets/postgresql-lab-setup.sql.
-- Design project-specific tables here; never run destructive resets in a production database.

-- Example report pattern:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, COALESCE(SUM(o.total_amount), 0) AS spend
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name
ORDER BY spend DESC, c.customer_id;
acceptance_notes: Keep the row meaning of every table and report explicit.
Validate referential integrity and edge cases with synthetic data.
Use transaction tests for multi-step changes; don't claim concurrency safety without a multi-session test.
Document all PostgreSQL-specific features and possible portability alternatives.
deliverables_review: ER diagram or schema notes, schema scripts, synthetic seed data, query library, validation checklist, and README.
assessment_criteria: Correctness, data integrity, query readability, reproducibility, and documented design decisions.
